simple.meaning: קָשֶׁה (qâsheh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “severe (in various applications).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 36 times across Genesis, Exodus, Deuteronomy, Judges, 1 Samuel, and 8 more, beginning at Genesis 42:7. Its contexts include family, land, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קָשֶׁה (H7186).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: קָשֶׁה (qâsheh) / H7186 is traced through Genesis 42:7, Genesis 42:30, Exodus 1:14, Exodus 6:9 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.usage: churlish, cruel, grievous, hard((-hearted), thing), heavy, impudent, obstinate, prevailed, rough(-ly), sore, sorrowful, stiff(necked), stubborn, in trouble.

occurrences.englishText: Joseph saw his brothers, and he recognized them, but acted like a stranger to them, and spoke roughly with them. He said to them, “Where did you come from?”
“The man, the lord of the land, spoke roughly with us, and took us for spies of the country.
and they made their lives bitter with hard service in mortar and in brick, and in all kinds of service in the field, all their service, in which they ruthlessly made them serve.
Moses spoke so to the children of Israel, but they didn’t listen to Moses for anguish of spirit, and for cruel bondage.
They judged the people at all times. They brought the hard cases to Moses, but every small matter they judged themselves.
Yahweh said to Moses, “I have seen these people, and behold, they are a stiff-necked people.
Go to a land flowing with milk and honey; but I will not go up among you, for you are a stiff-necked people, lest I consume you on the way.”

Yahweh had said to Moses, “Tell the children of Israel, ‘You are a stiff-necked people. If I were to go up among you for one moment, I would consume you. Therefore now take off your jewelry from you, that I may know what to do to you.’ ”

He said, “If now I have found favor in your sight, Lord, please let the Lord go among us, even though this is a stiff-necked people; pardon our iniquity and our sin, and take us for your inheritance.”
Know therefore that Yahweh your God doesn’t give you this good land to possess for your righteousness, for you are a stiff-necked people.
Furthermore Yahweh spoke to me, saying, “I have seen this people, and behold, it is a stiff-necked people.
The Egyptians mistreated us, afflicted us, and imposed hard labor on us.
For I know your rebellion and your stiff neck. Behold, while I am yet alive with you today, you have been rebellious against Yahweh. How much more after my death?

But when the judge was dead, they turned back, and dealt more corruptly than their fathers in following other gods to serve them and to bow down to them. They didn’t cease what they were doing, or give up their stubborn ways.
The hand of the children of Israel prevailed more and more against Jabin the king of Canaan, until they had destroyed Jabin king of Canaan.
Hannah answered, “No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit. I have not been drinking wine or strong drink, but I poured out my soul before Yahweh.
Then David said to Jonathan, “Who will tell me if your father answers you roughly?”
Now the name of the man was Nabal; and the name of his wife Abigail. This woman was intelligent and had a beautiful face; but the man was surly and evil in his doings. He was of the house of Caleb.
The battle was very severe that day; and Abner was beaten, and the men of Israel, before David’s servants.
I am weak today, though anointed king. These men, the sons of Zeruiah are too hard for me. May Yahweh reward the evildoer according to his wickedness.”
“Your father made our yoke difficult. Now therefore make the hard service of your father, and his heavy yoke which he put on us, lighter, and we will serve you.”
The king answered the people roughly, and abandoned the counsel of the old men which they had given him,
So when Ahijah heard the sound of her feet as she came in at the door, he said, “Come in, Jeroboam’s wife! Why do you pretend to be another? For I am sent to you with heavy news.
“Your father made our yoke grievous: now therefore make the grievous service of your father, and his heavy yoke which he put on us, lighter, and we will serve you.”
The king answered them roughly; and king Rehoboam abandoned the counsel of the old men,
Didn’t I weep for him who was in trouble?
So that your beloved may be delivered,
It will happen in the day that Yahweh will give you rest from your sorrow, from your trouble, and from the hard service in which you were made to serve,
I will give over the Egyptians into the hand of a cruel lord. A fierce king will rule over them,” says the Lord, Yahweh of Armies.
A grievous vision is declared to me. The treacherous man deals treacherously, and the destroyer destroys. Go up, Elam; attack! I have stopped all of Media’s sighing.
In that day, Yahweh with his hard and great and strong sword will punish leviathan, the fleeing serpent, and leviathan the twisted serpent; and he will kill the dragon that is in the sea.
In measure, when you send them away, you contend with them. He has removed them with his rough blast in the day of the east wind.
Because I knew that you are obstinate,
The children are impudent and stiff-hearted. I am sending you to them, and you shall tell them, ‘This is what the Lord* The word translated “Lord” is “Adonai.” Yahweh says.’
But the house of Israel will not listen to you, for they will not listen to me; for all the house of Israel are obstinate* Literally, have a hard forehead and hard-hearted.
